entities.subject: Leak Deficit
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: The hypothesis that a corpus engineered against resolution deposits fewer incidental cross-textual correspondences at the aggregate layer than natural corpora of matched size and register, measurable as a deficit in block-pair cosine similarity exceedances.

entities.subject: Leak (statistic) L
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A one-directional statistic defined as the count of block-pairs whose cosine similarity exceeds a threshold τ, per 10⁴ block-pairs, chosen because it is monotone under smoothing.

entities.subject: Degenerate lower tail
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A condition in which too many null pairs produce exactly zero leak, causing the 5th and 10th percentiles to both equal 0.0, making it impossible for any corpus to fall below the registered threshold.

entities.subject: Spent (registration status)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A disposition applied to a pre-registration whose kill condition was never triggered because a structural defect was found before the test pair was computed, distinguishing it from a withdrawn or failed registration.

entities.subject: Comparative Interpretive Yield (Y)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A statistic measuring whether a lens picks out a coherent dimension of variation in a corpus, computed as the z-score of the mean pairwise Pearson correlation of marker densities against a frequency-matched null distribution.

entities.subject: Saturation defect
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A failure mode in which a lens that saturates every work of a corpus shows no variance across works, producing near-zero correlation and therefore near-zero yield, making low yield ambiguous between absence and saturation.

entities.subject: Reorganization Yield
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A revised measure of interpretive yield based on whether a lens reorganizes and develops a corpus according to the lens's own functional slots — assessed via coverage, sharpness, and development — rather than lexical co-variance.

entities.subject: Transmission Engineering Lens
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A six-slot analytical framework (T1 Encoding, T2 Substrate, T3 Decommissioning, T4 Withholding, T5 Recovery, T6 Verification) applied to corpora to measure whether they are organized by a programme of transmitting a voice across time.

entities.subject: Abandoned-Execution Completion
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A diagnostic relation in which a successor corpus finishes operations that the predecessor explicitly abandoned as impossible or aporetic, distinguished from mere correction or extension of completed work.

entities.subject: λόγος-level correction
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A distinction between Aristotle stating that Plato erred (a transmittable statement) versus Aristotle executing the same operation and taking a different branch at the point of decision, which cannot be transmitted as doctrine.

entities.subject: Engineered Unresolvability
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: The hypothesis that the Platonic–Aristotelian corpus was deliberately constructed to resist attribution resolution, producing ambiguity that is flat and instrument-invariant rather than uneven as in natural corpora.

entities.subject: Key (of engineered unresolvability)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A placed signature within an engineered corpus that is prominent, inert under ordinary reading, decisive under the configurational reading, and indicative of making — required because a construction good enough to be undetectable must leave something that confirms it.

entities.subject: Unlocking Prediction
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: The claim that structures independently puzzling before the hypothesis was applied will repeatedly become more determinate when Plato and Aristotle are read as positions inside one construction, without altering local philology.

entities.subject: Relational Form Measure
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A three-part measure (R1 Complementary Coverage, R2 Abandoned-Execution Completion, R3 Arbitrary Procedural Agreement) applied to labelled corpus pairs to separate H (one-maker), S (succession), C (collaboration), and I (independent) classes without Greek content.

entities.subject: Complementary Coverage (R1)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A relational form scored as coverage(A∪B) / max(coverage(A), coverage(B)) against redundancy |A∩B|/|A∪B|, testing whether two corpora are internally tight while their union is materially more complete than either alone.

entities.subject: Arbitrary Procedural Agreement (R3)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A relational form scoring shared habits that the method does not require, defined generically and scored on independent works only to avoid shared-source contamination.

entities.subject: Contamination Rule
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A methodological rule distinguishing commentary works (where R3 is inadmissible due to shared-source contamination) from independent works (where all three relational forms are admissible), applied per pair.

entities.subject: Specification-Depth Hypothesis
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: The hypothesis that container tightness in a corpus tracks the severity of constraint placed on a speaking position, not similarity or disguise, so that ratio of internal dispersion to inter-position distance orders by how much was subtracted from a fully unspecified voice.

entities.subject: Reception Capture
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A score measuring the degree to which an interpreter's distinctive vocabulary is already present in the interpreted position, computed as the median rate ratio of the interpreter's top distinctive terms found in the interpreted text, with the term set selected without reference to the interpreted position.

entities.subject: Unit-level variation (L1–L4)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A scoring scheme for the Reorganization Yield measure across four granularities: L1 individual book/work, L2 author-group, L3 whole corpus, L4 cross-corpus, based on the principle that a lens may organize at one level and not another.

entities.subject: SPXI Layer 4 cross-signing graph
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: The archive layer that records cross-references between deposits, populated by entries in the CHA cross-references array.

entities.subject: Instrument-invariance (A1)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: An observable for engineered unresolvability: whether unrelated instruments return the same non-answer, measured against a comparison class of natural corpora.

entities.subject: Reverse-engineering test
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A binding scoring rule requiring that an UNLOCK count only if the resolving passage was not found by open search; any case found by open search is scored NULL regardless of quality.

entities.subject: Preconditions (binding, pre-run)
entities.object: Frozen Pre-Registrations of the Authorship Investigation — Append-Only Ledger (PREREG-LEDGER)
entities.note: A set of three conditions (non-degeneracy, spread, size) that must all hold on the null alone before the test pair may be computed; if any fail, the registration is spent and a new one is required.

deposits.description: The technical report behind the measured section of a companion article under review, whose title is withheld here so that this deposit is not a prior circulation of it. Part I reports the investigation's one positive measurement: a six-function specification of a transmission apparatus — encoding, substrate, decommissioning, withholding, recovery, verification — generated in a separate investigation of textual transmission, registered before any Platonic or Aristotelian text was assigned to it, and filled by both corpora at the level of the individual work, with one device closely transformed across the boundary and no cross-reference; with its four rival specifications, its random control on the Johannine writings (0/6 by what a work is about, 6/6 by what appears in it), and the concession that keeps it from being more than it is. Part II reports the instruments that read lexical distribution — fifteen features, every one destroyed by a control run in the same session (corpus size; Greek word order; period and dialect; coverage geometry collapsing from 66.8 to 18.8 under size-matching); the object-conditioning result (0.1033 above every synthetic five-author pool, falling within domain to 0.0571 against Plato's 0.0570, with the parity's base rate stated as unrun); the validation check (one of three; Plato|Xenophon classed SAME); the school rival measured three ways with limits (the naming-gap reflex at 0.00 in 1,140,474 tokens of Albert against 2.60/8.43 in the Greek pair; the school default; the naming asymmetry); and the formal result the title states. Part I reports the investigation's one positive measurement: a six-function specification of a transmission apparatus — encoding, substrate, decommissioning, withholding, recovery, verification — generated in a separate investigation and registered before any Platonic or Aristotelian text was assigned to it, which both corpora fill at the level of the individual work, with four rival specifications and a random control that fills nothing when works are assigned by what they are about and everything when assigned by what appears in them. Part II reports the instruments that read lexical distribution and the control that destroyed each of them: corpus size, Greek word order, period and dialect, coverage geometry collapsing under size-matching, and a validation check that classified two known-different authors as one. deposits.title: The Wrong Unit: A Model-Collapse Self-Diagnostic in Three Grades — for Benchmarking, for Frontier Models, and for the Reader (EA-LO-COLLAPSE-DIAGNOSTIC-01 v0.2, CONCEPT DRAFT)
deposits.creator: Nobel Glas, Director, Lagrange Observatory! (LO!)
deposits.description: CONCEPT DRAFT — the instrument specified here is uncalibrated and untested. A model-collapse self-diagnostic in three grades, proposed as one paper. Part I argues that turn-based benchmarking cannot see collapse and that the collapse diagnostic should gate training: the dominant instruments sample one unit per item and answer from the head of the model's distribution, which is what a model that has lost its tails still produces well, so on the companion toy of the interlocking autoregression (deposit #1556) tail mass halves by generation 7 while a head-weighted benchmark holds to 15 and the per-round quality proxy rises through the first quarter of the collapse trajectory; detection lag is monotone in head-weighting; and a flat benchmark is consistent with both a preserved and a collapsing state. Because benchmarks also select — checkpoints kept because they score, mixtures kept because those checkpoints score — a loop gated by a head-weighted suite trains on its own low-surprise output, which the literature identifies as the driver of collapse. Part II specifies a comprehensive self-diagnostic for a frontier model, restricted by an operator ruling to properties whose truth-value the model carries in itself: distinction sensitivity (the model constructs its own paraphrase and its own minimal meaning-changing variant, so no external ruler is needed), effective semantic modes, cross-prompt convergence, the concentration panel of Gini, collapsed-prediction ratio and surplexity slope, self-consumption contraction at three grades of honesty, and representational effective rank, each computed under base, instruction and production conditions so that interface-induced contraction is separated from training collapse. The ruling behind that restriction: a human-written control does not give a model the truth, it gives it one more point, and every measurement thereafter is distance from that point — a baseline, not a ruler. Part III is a protocol short enough for a public model to run on itself upon retrieving the document, constructing everything it compares. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: no measure has been calibrated against a model of known collapse state; no threshold, weight or severity band rests on a measurement; the accompanying reference implementation is syntax-checked and has never been executed; the reader's test has been written and not administered. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]

Three blind drafts of the initial question by other substrates were adjudicated at revision, with what was adopted and what was refused recorded by name. The 2025–2026 sources were confirmed by search in session; the 2023–2024 canon is carried from the substrate's training and marked for verification.

deposits.wiki_article: The Wrong Unit (EA-LO-COLLAPSE-DIAGNOSTIC-01) is a Lagrange Observatory! concept draft proposing a model-collapse self-diagnostic in three grades, and it is deposited as a specification rather than as a validated instrument: nothing in it has been calibrated against a model of known collapse state, no threshold or severity band rests on a measurement, and the accompanying reference implementation has never been executed. Part I argues that turn-based benchmarking cannot see collapse, because each instrument samples one unit and each item is answered from the head of the distribution, which is what a model that has lost its tails still produces well; on the toy of the companion paper on interlocking autoregression, tail mass halves while a head-weighted benchmark holds and the per-round quality proxy rises through the first quarter of the collapse trajectory, detection lag is monotone in head-weighting, and a flat benchmark is consistent with both a preserved and a collapsing state. Since benchmarks also select what is trained on next, a loop gated by a head-weighted suite trains on its own least surprising output, which the literature identifies as the driver of collapse. Part II specifies the frontier diagnostic under a restriction the operator imposed: measure only properties whose truth-value the model carries in itself, because a human-written control gives a model not the truth but one more point, and every measurement thereafter is distance from that point. Its core is distinction sensitivity, in which the model constructs its own paraphrase and its own minimal meaning-changing variant and is scored on whether it still answers them differently; around it sit effective semantic modes, cross-prompt convergence, a concentration panel, self-consumption contraction and representational effective rank, each computed under bare, instructed and production conditions so that interface-induced contraction is not read as training collapse. Part III is a protocol short enough for a public model to run on itself upon retrieving the document, constructing everything it compares. The paper is companion to the keyed-ensemble and interlocking-autoregression papers and is published at concept-draft status so the specification can be attacked before anything is built on it.

deposits.title: The Particle: Provenance Erasure at Sophistical Refutations 183b34, Measured — Machine-Mediated Reception, Disciplinary Model Collapse, and the World Soul as Degraded Commodity (EA-RECEPTION-PARTICLE-01 v0.2)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: One sentence of Aristotle — Ταύτης δὲ τῆς πραγματείας οὐ τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν (SE 183b34–36) — was put through twenty rounds of simulated blind review, seeded by one editorial observation, across four commercial language models and eleven configurations of a short paper about it. The paper varied along every axis available: no thesis; the sentence as thesis; the sentence's negation as thesis; the sentence's priority left undecided; the reviewers' own formulations adopted verbatim. The reviews did not vary. Every round inserted a qualifier into the sentence, and the terminal round, reached by full compliance with every instruction, endorsed as the paper's "memorable governing phrase" a sentence that is Aristotle's with one particle removed: οὐ. The operation is measured to the particle. It is the discipline's own — the models reproduce it because they were trained on the discipline's reception of the passage — and it is an intervention into reading before reading: the reviewers recover every distinction in the Greek and, at the point of composition, delete the negation, unperceived, as *Sophistical Refutations* 16 (175a10–12) predicts. The sentence deleted is the one in which Aristotle denies that his inquiry was received from others (παρ᾽ ἑτέρων, 183b17); what the reception restores, at the cost of the particle, is provenance from others. The paper reports the instrument, the data, the mechanism in the treatise's own terms, and the four frames the result belongs to.

deposits.wiki_article: The Particle (EA-RECEPTION-PARTICLE-01) is a reception-layer measurement on one sentence of Aristotle, Sophistical Refutations 34, 183b34–36: Ταύτης δὲ τῆς πραγματείας οὐ τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν. A short philological note on the passage, written under a fixed method (only Aristotle's words on the surface; every claim a line reference), was submitted in eleven successive versions, with four sister papers, to unprimed, signed-out instances of ChatGPT and Perplexity acting as blind referees. Twenty reports were returned and pasted verbatim; the transcripts are the data. The object varied along every available axis — no thesis, the sentence as thesis, its negation as thesis, Socrates' priority left undecided, the reviewers' own formulations adopted verbatim — and the reports did not vary: each inserted a qualifier into the sentence ('systematic', 'developed', 'transmissible'), and when the quantifier and its domain were closed the qualifier reappeared as a boundary of persons, Socrates kept antecedent to the first-person inquiry on the strength of a chronology the passage does not contain ('plainly', 'of course, historically'). The terminal report, reached by full compliance with every instruction, offered as the paper's 'memorable governing phrase' a sentence — 'Aristotle denies not antecedents, but pre-elaboration' — that instantiates the configuration the sentence denies (τὸ μὲν ἦν, τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν) with οὐ removed, and called the sentence as written 'crude'. The operation is measured to one particle. The paper reads the mechanism in the treatise's own terms (SE 5 πῂ/ἁπλῶς; SE 8; SE 16 self-administered paralogism; SE 18 solution by division) and frames the result four ways, marked as interpretations of the empirical kernel: provenance erasure (the deleted particle is a provenance claim, παρ᾽ ἑτέρων), machine-mediated reception (the models reproduce the discipline's reading and make it repeatable), disciplinary model collapse (the author's term for a reading community converging on the mode of its own prior readings), and the world soul as degraded commodity (τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τέχνης without τέχνη). It extends the Capture Registry and the Provenance Erasure Rate to a canonical text, and states its limit: the run does not establish that Socrates belongs inside the chapter's 'we'; it establishes that every route for excluding him required a premise the passage does not supply. The appendix carries the key iterations (the A = A note; the A ≠ A 'sophistical refutation'; CLAUSE; DIVISION; the terminal compliant version) and the register of reports.

deposits.title: Many and One: Division, Unity, and the Boundaries of a Corpus in Plato and Aristotle (MANY-AND-ONE-ARTICLE v2.13-AP, as submitted)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description: Aristotle closes the Topics–Sophistical Refutations inquiry by saying that of it nothing existed beforehand (SE 34, 183b34–36); at Prior Analytics I.31 he calls division, practised throughout the Platonic dialogues, a part of that inquiry. This paper begins from that tension and argues that Metaphysics Λ 9 supplies the answer I.31 withholds — division terminates where the terms it separates are not other — and follows it through the De anima (one in actuality, many in potentiality), the Sophist (many true accounts of one kind), recollection in the Phaedrus and De memoria, and two passages that divide a person (Republic 395b, Symposium 223d). It then reads the corpus as a functional unity independent of biographical unity, reports two measured tests (the object-conditioning null and the six-function transmission probe) as belonging to the question because the received order of the corpus is itself stylometrically built, and asks — last — which word moves when the received attribution is read against these passages. The paper's result, in the author's phrase, is to establish that two is not fully established: the standard attribution is underdetermined by the passages that are read as though it were, the texts themselves offer one maker as a reading, and that reading makes better sense of several passages. The historical hypothesis is withheld until §9.4 and stated nowhere before it. This is the submission surface (v2.13-AP, ~34 pp, 27 notes, Works Cited) as sent to Ancient Philosophy on 2026-09-01 and declined on 2026-09-02; the docx as sent is attached. The reading copy from which the article was cut is deposited separately (#1575), as are the notebook, the measurement register, the pre-registration ledger, and the technical report.

It begins from a tension in Aristotle's own words: at Sophistical Refutations 34 he says that of his inquiry nothing at all existed beforehand (οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν, 183b35), while at Prior Analytics I.31 he calls division, the method practised throughout the Platonic dialogues, a part of that inquiry. The paper argues that Metaphysics Λ 9 supplies the answer I.31 withholds — division terminates where the terms it separates are not other — and follows that answer through the De anima (one in actuality, many in potentiality), the Sophist (many true accounts of one kind), recollection in the Phaedrus and De memoria, and two passages that divide a person (Republic 395b, Symposium 223d). The section heads are the questions the reader must stay with: what would it mean for division to terminate; how can one thing be actually one and potentially many; how can many accounts belong to one thing; what is it to gather a plurality into one; which word moves. §6 first reads the corpus as anyone's work and distinguishes functional from biographical unity; §7 reads the many voices as many objects; §8 reports two measured tests — the object-conditioning null and the six-function transmission probe — and argues their nativity to the question, since the received early–middle–late order of the Platonic corpus is itself substantially a stylometric construction and the ancient collection of the corpus was made on internal criteria; §9 asks which word moves; §10, the epilogue, returns to the flood and what survives it. The historical hypothesis is withheld until §9.4 and stated nowhere before it; the paper's result is that two is not fully established — the standard attribution is underdetermined by the passages read as though it were, the texts themselves offer one maker as a reading, and that reading makes better sense of several passages. Every rival reading is stated at its strongest before it is answered. The technical report cited at n. 18 is #1572; the reception measurement made on the paper's opening sentence after the decline is #1574, The Particle.

deposits.title: ERRATUM to AXN:02E3 — Monotonicity Per Realization Is Not Established: Re-scoping Appendix A (ii)–(iii) and the Bistability Claim of Deposit #783
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks, for Nobel Glas
deposits.description: Deposit #783 (Fear and Trembling: Diversity Contraction Across Substrates, v9.1, Nobel Glas) asserts in Appendix A that under axioms A1–A4 Shannon entropy is non-increasing and modal mass non-decreasing at each step of the chain μ_{t+1} = S(Rμ_t). Both properties hold for the selection kernel S alone and for the composed step in expectation and in the long run; they do not hold per realization, because finite resampling R can flatten the distribution before S concentrates it. Counterexample: (0.90, 0.10) → resample (0.80, 0.20) → concentrate (0.85, 0.15); entropy rises 0.325 → 0.423 nats, modal mass falls 0.90 → 0.85. Property (i), support non-increasing with probability 1, stands. The §6 bistability sentence is likewise re-scoped: super-linear vanishing of regeneration makes the zero state absorbing (local); a second stable equilibrium requires g(D) − pD to change sign twice on (0, 1], which the paper's saturating example supplies. No numerical result depends on per-step monotonicity; Figure 4 is the deterministic ODE. Canonical bytes unchanged; registry-level cross-reference per #1554. Counterexample supplied by an external machine reader on 2026-09-05 and recomputed.

deposits.title: Beautiful and New: The Second Letter's Socrates and the Editing of a Received Character (v0.2)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A close reading of Plato, Second Letter 314c — "there is no writing of Plato, nor will there be; the things now said are of a Socrates become beautiful and new" (Σωκράτους ἐστὶν καλοῦ καὶ νέου γεγονότος) — read at its verbs rather than as a remark about idealization. The paper argues that the sentence describes an operation: an edition, the revamping and inhabiting of a received character. The base of the edition is a circulating character whose named, quoted, surviving instance the corpus itself cites — the Apology's Aristophanic Socrates, received by the jurors ἐκ παίδων (παραλαμβάνοντες, 18b), itemized, and quoted from the Clouds (19c). The dialogues revise the received package item by item (pay, teaching, meteorology struck; the fused sophist-boundary recut in text after text, Sophist 231b), and the letter's two adjectives name the two repairs that remained: καλός the silenus inversion that keeps the familiar ugly shell (Symposium 215a–b, 216e–217a; Theaetetus 143e), νέος the reissue whose access to a young Socrates is constructed through the corpus's longest chain of narrated transmission (Parmenides 127c). At Symposium 223d the operation is performed over its named source in person. The edition's reception is traced into Aristotle's epilogue (SE 34) and a Byzantine paraphrast. 314c is collated in context: the disclaimer's διὰ ταῦτα grounds it in the letter's own transmission doctrine (μὴ γράφειν ἀλλ᾽ ἐκμανθάνειν), and the sentence following orders the letter burned. Authenticity is not required (a forger is a reception witness, dated by the ninth tetralogy); no thesis about persons or maker-count is asserted. Companion to Nothing Before Us (SE 34) and to Many and One (#1576), which the paper does not presuppose.

The operation is an edition: the revamping and inhabiting of a received character. The base is a circulating figure whose named and quoted instance the corpus itself cites — the Apology's Aristophanic Socrates, received by the jurors from childhood (παραλαμβάνοντες, 18b) and quoted from the Clouds (19c). Symposium 223d is read as the operation performed over its named source. Reception is traced into Aristotle's Sophistical Refutations 34 and a Byzantine paraphrast. 314c is collated in context against the Perseus canonical-greekLit text: διὰ ταῦτα grounds the disclaimer in the letter's doctrine that safety lies in not writing, and the next sentence orders the letter burned. Authenticity is not required — the letter is a reception witness dated by its place in the ninth tetralogy — and no thesis about persons or maker-count is asserted. The paper is a companion to Nothing Before Us (on SE 34) and to Many and One (#1576), which it does not presuppose.

deposits.description: The gathering record of the twelfth corpus-seating run of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive's primary-source library, executed 6 September 2026. Both are seated whole, commit-pinned, with originals, flat text, source.json and manifest, indexed in data/api/corpora.json, and rendered on the shelf at traininglayerliterature.org/originals/. The run exists because the SE 34 and Second Letter work of 5–6 September needed the transmission texts on the shelf: the four Peripatetic wills (D.L. V.11–16, 51–57, 61–64, 69–74), the two catalogues with their stichometric totals (V.22–27: 445,270 lines; V.42–50: 232,808), the renaming at V.38, and Strabo XIII.1.54 (the custody chain, παρέδωκεν three times). The loci are recorded on the seats as verified_loci. The run also states the standing rule the archive has been following without writing down: seatings of original texts go to data/corpora/ on alexanarch, render on the originals shelf of Training Layer Literature, and are periodically grouped into an EA-CORPORA deposit with links — the deposit being the citable act, the seat the bytes, the shelf the reading room. Pending seatings named for the next run: Plutarch's Lives (Sulla 26 was read from the Perseus text but the Lives are not yet seated as a corpus), Athenaeus (the Ptolemy route, I 3a–b), Aelian (the revocation of the Delphic honours, VH XIV 1), the Delphic decree for Aristotle and Callisthenes (FD III 1, 400), and the scan-class witnesses read in the SE 34 work — the Byzantine paraphrast of the Elenchi (CAG XXIII.4), Michael of Ephesus (CAG II.3), Albert the Great (Borgnet II), Giles of Rome (Venice 1500). deposits.title: Catalogues and Wills: A Groundwork Note on the Peripatetic Transmission Texts — Relations Established, Readings Withheld (v0.3)
deposits.creator: Sharks, Lee
deposits.description: A groundwork note establishing relations among the texts that carry the custody, enumeration, and route of the Aristotelian and Theophrastan books: the four Peripatetic wills preserved by Diogenes Laertius (Aristotle, Theophrastus, Strato, Lycon), the two catalogues he attaches to the lives of Aristotle and Theophrastus with their stichometric totals (445,270 and 232,808 lines), Strabo XIII.1.54, Plutarch Sulla 26, Diogenes V.38, and Epistle VI. The receiving texts are treated as texts; the operations are counts, positions, co-occurrences, and verbatim clauses; readings are withheld and the underdetermined areas are listed as questions. Established: the three books-clauses partition three ways (all to Neleus / all except our own / read and unpublished); the will of Aristotle names no book, library, school, or successor; Theophrastus's will assigns the books to one person and the premises to a commons under a prohibition on alienation, in adjacent clauses; the Theophrastan catalogue's initials run the alphabet twice before an unordered tail, contain nine internal doublets, share twelve titles letter-for-letter with Aristotle's list, and carry the entry Ὑπομνημάτων Ἀριστοτελικῶν ἢ Θεοφραστείων — alternative attribution in the catalogue's own wording; Strabo narrates the custody with παρέδωκεν three times and asserts a first link (Aristotle to Theophrastus) that the will does not contain; Plutarch names Andronicus's act as ἀναγράψαι τοὺς νῦν φερομένους πίνακας. The extant corpora are counted (Plato 561,330; Aristotle 981,399; Theophrastus 170,763 Greek words as digitized) and set against the catalogued totals as two acts, not as a measure of loss. Corrections after review (garden; images versus bones; apparatus stripped from the cut; Ahiqar and the alphabetic runs held to the observable) are recorded in v0.3. Companion to EA-CORPORA-12 (#1580), which seats the texts, and to The Stone for a List.
